protocol.hypothesis: Native address channels are fixed damped Fourier traces of a common scalar activity: z_j(k+1)=lambda_j*z_j(k)+b_j*x(k+1). lambda and b may be unknown, complex, and learned.
protocol.necessary_identity: For every pair j,l, [dz_j(k+1),dz_j(k),dz_l(k+1),dz_l(k)] has complex rank <=3. This condition even allows complex x and arbitrary lambda, without fitting either.
protocol.no_intervention: Use actual model trajectories only; compare with a generated known trace as a measurement control.
protocol.pair_scope: Test each cell separately, allowing different hypothetical lambda/b across cells; fixed across its recorded time window.
protocol.pair_rejection: sigma4/sigma1 > max(1e-3,10*conservative_FP32_noise_scale); exclude channels with RMS increment below 1e-4 of RMS level
protocol.approximate_fit: Fixed lambda and real rank-r innovations across training puzzles; fresh activity coefficients allowed freely on every holdout step. This is structural reconstruction, not forecasting.
protocol.normalization: RMS of complex increments in training data, per channel. This fixed rescaling leaves lambda invariant.
protocol.exact_acceptance: Necessary rank identities and holdout residual <=1e-4; synthetic control must recover frequency to 1e-3 rad/block.
protocol.approximate_threshold: Report error continuously. <=0.1 relative residual norm is a predeclared useful-approximation target, not mathematical identity.
protocol.limitation: An unconstrained independent complex activity per channel permits any chosen lambda by definition; it does not identify a temporal frequency from v1.1 alone.

control.purpose: Verify the procedure recovers a true common-drive damped rotation from FP32 traces; this is not an untrained-model comparison
